title: Excavations in Palestine and Trans-Jordan, 1940-1: 'Ain Karim, Church of St. John the Baptist
author: (round-up; clearances directed by S. J. Saller)
location_note: West of the church and monastery of St. John the Baptist, 'Ain Karim; no map reference; placed by name. p. 113 inferred (leaf before p. 114, after the Abu Ghosh paragraph that opens the round-up).
reading: full (the span includes the map figure on p. 114)
notes: June-Sept. 1941 clearances: a rock-cut stepped chamber with Herodian pottery, early Byzantine wine and oil presses, two Byzantine chapels with mosaics, Crusader and later walls. Function of the stepped chamber not stated; INFERENCE: its steps leading to a trough-like depression recall a stepped pool, but it is coded as an artificial underground chamber (cave_with_finds), not as a ritual bath.

features.subtype: rock-cut chamber reached by five steps in a rock-sunk shaft, round-arched door, two broad steps down to a trough-like depression (function not given)
features.period: Herodian pottery in the depression; 'the oldest monument found'
features.quote: A rock-cut chamber is the oldest monument found

features.site: west of the church, under the northern chapel
features.subtype: wine and oil presses: system of basins, channels and vats with mosaic floors
features.quote: A system of basins, channels, and vats associated with mosaic pavements
